name: Roseanna Robinson
bio: Roseanna Robinson was a Black pacifist (a member of Peacemakers) jailed for a year and a day in 1960 for refusing to file income-tax returns because the money would be used 'for military and war purposes.' Carried into court in a wheelchair, she went on a hunger strike and was force-fed at the Alderson federal prison before her release that May.
charges: Willful failure to file income tax — war-tax resistance
sentence: A year and a day (released May 1960)

name: Marjorie Swann
bio: Marjorie Swann was a pacifist who served a six-month federal prison sentence for the 1959 'Omaha Action' protest against construction of the Mead, Nebraska intercontinental missile base. One of 18 arrested and seven jailed, she was the last released, returning home in January 1960.
charges: Trespass / obstruction — antinuclear protest at the Mead missile base

name: Donald Martin
bio: Donald Martin was a 20-year-old pacifist of the Committee for Non-Violent Action ('Polaris Action') who was jailed on trespassing charges after swimming out to and boarding the nuclear submarine Ethan Allen at its launching in Groton, Connecticut in November 1960, in protest against the Polaris missile program.
charges: Trespassing — boarding the Polaris submarine Ethan Allen in protest

name: Bill Henry
bio: Bill Henry was a 27-year-old Committee for Non-Violent Action pacifist jailed with Donald Martin on trespassing charges after the two swam to and boarded the nuclear submarine Ethan Allen at its November 1960 launching in Groton, Connecticut, in the 'Polaris Action' protest against nuclear-missile submarines.
charges: Trespassing — boarding the Polaris submarine Ethan Allen in protest

name: Lucia Shapiro
bio: Lucia Shapiro was one of 26 demonstrators arrested at City Hall Park in New York on May 3, 1960 for refusing to take shelter during the compulsory 'Operation Alert' civil-defense drill — a protest against nuclear-war preparations. She was sentenced to five days in jail.
charges: Refusing to take shelter during a compulsory civil-defense drill

name: Anne Morrissett
bio: Anne Morrissett was among the 26 protesters arrested at City Hall Park in New York on May 3, 1960 for refusing to take shelter during the compulsory civil-defense drill, invoking 'a tradition of defying the law and taking the consequences.' She was sentenced to five days in jail.
charges: Refusing to take shelter during a compulsory civil-defense drill

name: June Croll Gordon
affiliation: Emma Lazarus Federation of Women's Clubs
bio: June Croll Gordon was the executive secretary of the Emma Lazarus Federation of Women's Clubs and a former secretary of the Anti-Nazi Federation. In August 1960 the Immigration Service issued a deportation order against her on a charge of having entered the U.S. illegally from Canada in 1928 — a technical pretext widely seen as targeting a left-wing Jewish civic leader.
charges: Walter-McCarran Act deportation — alleged illegal 1928 entry

name: Hamish Scott MacKay
bio: Hamish Scott MacKay was a 55-year-old Portland, Oregon carpenter, in the U.S. since 1928, who had led Depression-era Workers' Alliance demonstrations for jobs. Denied citizenship in 1935 as an alleged Communist, he was deported to Canada on Nov. 18, 1960 after an 11-year fight, the Supreme Court having refused a stay 5-4.
charges: Walter-McCarran Act deportation — alleged Communist / Workers' Alliance activity

name: Jose Santiago
bio: Jose Santiago was a Puerto Rican patriot and former Communist, a leader of the Provisional Organizing Committee to Reconstitute a Marxist-Leninist Party. In 1960, after years of deportation proceedings against his Canadian-born wife Jo Ann tied to his radical politics, Canada refused to admit him and the family was forced into exile in Cuba — what the Guardian called the first Puerto Rican family thus exiled from the U.S.
charges: Deportation / exile pressure tied to his radical political leadership
sentence: Exiled with his family to Cuba
